output.brief: The Android login drop is almost certainly caused by a new Corvane edge rule, not release 6.14. Corvane's 3 March rule-pack update added a rule (AUTO-LIB-17). It blocks password-login requests from the nettle-http library when they carry no edge session cookie. The Android app uses that library for every API call. The rule started blocking at 10:41 UTC, and the added failures are HTTP 403 rejections that began that same minute on every app version, including 6.11 and older. Failure rates were the same for phones with and without the March security patch. Quick-unlock is unaffected. About 41,000 blocked installs, 92% of which had logged in successfully in the previous 90 days, look like real customers rather than bots. So I would not roll back 6.14. I would also not raise bot sensitivity or exclude blocked attempts from the KPI, since both would worsen the problem or hide it. Next step: ask Corvane to set the 3 March rules to log-only on the mobile password path, keeping the other protections on. Then confirm in telemetry that Android password success returns to about 96%. I'm confident in the cause. The link between the drop and the extra calls is plausible but not proven, because call reason codes are unreliable.
